derivationRules.door: Door height 2.2 units (Look Bible §5; VISUAL-PLAN REC-5). Door width 2 units = one MegaKit module opening (derived from the 2-unit native grid). Door face = the dominant axis of the primary-street vector (ties broken south-first, the camera side, then by the sign of dx). anchor_door is the threshold centre of that face (visual-plan/02 §5.2). anchor_sign sits centred on the same face 0.4 units above the door head (visual-plan/02 §5.2), i.e. 2.6 units up.
derivationRules.footprint: Width/depth in whole 2-unit modules, by the scale word in the building's recipe (visual-plan/02-asset-production.md §5.1): grand/large civic and hall class = 4 modules wide x 3 deep; small hall and workshop-scale = 3 x 2; homes = 2 x 2. District-plot parcel = 8 x 8 (the 10-unit cell minus a 1-unit street margin on each side). These module counts are a stated derivation rule for M4.11/M4.05 to ratify at build — no plan source states a per-building footprint number.
derivationRules.frontage: The primary street is the node's layout edge on the shortest path to the Plaza of Unity hub (the Plaza holds 7 of the layout's 14 authored edges). The frontage edge named in each spec is that edge, copied from the layout's edge list; the staged fill's Plaza edge is used for EMBER_DISTRICT_1_PLOT_30.
derivationRules.storeys: Stated only where a plan source states it. The College recipe names a timber upper floor over stone walls, so the College is 2. Every other building's floor count is unstated in every plan source, so storeys is null with the reason recorded — never inferred from a recipe's silhouette words.

dormantKitSeam.decision: NOT BUILT. D9's recommendation stands: D-9b ships (no health claim), the D-9a dormant variant kit is not produced. These specs fix base buildings only and presume no integrity-driven variation anywhere.
dormantKitSeam.seam: If the project owner ever approves D-9a, variants attach as separate dressing-layer GLBs (bld_<name>_var_<state>.glb) over the shared base building, per visual-plan/02-asset-production.md §5.4 — a scene change, not a remodel. The attach point in spec terms is the whole base footprint: the layer dresses the base spec's walls/roof within the same footprint and storeys. Naming the seam here is all this file does; no state geometry, palette, or prop is specified.
dormantKitSeam.statesProvenance: M4.15 (five states; blind-sort gate) with the four condition bands from the app's integrityTier and the repair state from plan/01-product-ux-plan.md ('Scaffolding in Ember means one thing: a civic work under recorded repair').

units.cellUnitsProvenance: build/visual/scene/scene.mjs header convention (1 v1 grid cell = 10 world units, Plaza at origin). No plan source converts v1 cells to units; visual-plan/01-rendering-scene.md §0's '1 unit = 1 grid cell' names the Office FloorData grid — the finer grid layout v3 adopts — not the v1 place grid. Recorded as a scale note for M4.11 in FOOTPRINTS.md, not resolved here.
units.gridOrientation: grid +y runs south (scene.mjs header; Town Hall at y=1 stands north). Door faces are compass directions in this frame; the canonical camera sits to the south (Look Bible §4).
units.moduleProvenance: MegaKit's native 2-unit grid is the physical constraint on building composition (visual-plan/VISUAL-PLAN.md REC-5, citing Production §0). Every footprint dimension below is a whole number of 2-unit modules.
units.unit: the build's world unit — the system the Look Bible rig and the scene scaffold both use (citizen 1.8, standard door 2.2)
